events.content:
Done. Category navigation is now prefetched per URL ahead of the click, with the existing `/catalog?category=...` URLs unchanged. Two small edits:

**`app/page.tsx`** — added `prefetch={true}` to each category `Link`. With `cacheComponents` enabled, this canary maps `prefetch={true}` to the `Full` fetch strategy (verified in `node_modules/next/dist/client/app-dir/link.js:373`): when a link enters the viewport, the router fetches that exact URL's complete response — including the `searchParams`-dependent heading and product list — and stores it in the client segment cache. Clicking then renders straight from that cache, so the `<Suspense>` "Loading category..." fallback never appears and no server round trip happens at click time. The default prefetch couldn't do this because reading `searchParams` makes the results section a runtime hole that's excluded from static (PPR) prefetches.

**`lib/data.ts`** — marked `getProducts` with `'use cache'` and `cacheLife('hours')`. This is what makes the full prefetch worthwhile: the product data gets a real cache lifetime, so the prefetched response is treated as fresh and reusable at click time (uncached dynamic data would make the response immediately stale), and repeat renders skip the 800ms fetch entirely.

Verified against a production build (`next build` succeeds, `/catalog` builds as a Partial Prerender) and a running `next start` server: the RSC payload for `/catalog?category=sale` contains "Products on sale" / "Canvas Tote" / "Travel Mug", the `featured` URL contains its own heading and products, and a warm request serves in ~15ms versus ~870ms cold. No headless browser was available in the sandbox, so the click-through itself wasn't exercised in a real browser — but the prefetch responses the browser would consume are confirmed complete and URL-specific.

Note the direct cold load of `/catalog` (typing the URL, no prefetch) still shows the fallback briefly while the first render streams in — that's inherent to a cold dynamic render and wasn't in scope; only the link-click path was made instant.
